titre: Indicatif du « Siècle en images » (marche, cordes)
licence: Création originale générée par IA pour le site
consigne:
Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir. Title music for a documentary series about nineteenth-century France. A dark, solemn orchestral march in the French Romantic style of the 1830s, played by a real acoustic symphony orchestra in a concert hall: no synthesizers, no drum kit, no modern film-trailer sound. Minor key (G minor), moderate march tempo around 72 bpm. A hammered march motif of 4 to 6 notes in the low brass (horns and trombones), with timpani and low strings playing pizzicato, stated immediately at the very first beat, then repeated. Variant: string-dominated, the low strings and violas drive the march with sharp pizzicato and then bowed accents, brass only reinforce the motif.
Structure (the endings are essential):
[0:00 - 0:11] The motif is stated twice, building quickly.
[0:11 - 0:12] A decisive cadence: one final full-orchestra tutti chord, fortissimo, on the tonic, with a single heavy timpani stroke, cut off cleanly.
[0:12 - 0:15] Complete silence.
[0:15 - 0:40] The march continues: the same motif developed, growing in intensity.
[0:40 - 0:55] Final restatement of the same motif by the full orchestra, ending with a decisive perfect cadence: two or three hammered tutti chords, the last one fortissimo with a timpani stroke, cut off cleanly, then silence.
